//: Configuration for the /human-review plugin (github.com/victorrentea/human-review).
The skill itself knows nothing about this project; everything petclinic-specific
lives here. A step this file does not describe is skipped and named under the
strip on the built page, which is the honest rendering of 'we have no such thing'.

//redraw: conceptual-model-patch.py draws what the code has and the map lacks,
in red, and leaves it red until a human lays it out. Named here so the
review page can offer to start over: restore the drawing to the base
and let the script draw the branch's additions again.
drawio.name: conceptual
drawio.//tested_against: What a unit test checks this drawing against; the review page says so under it.

//: The traced suites run against a stack of their own, never the host's: `up`
builds the commit under review WITH its own Grafana LGTM (--otel), so the
backend's and the browser's spans land in a Tempo nobody else exports to, and
two branches traced at once cannot draw each other's calls. --fresh drops the
instance's volumes, so every run starts from the seed: a diagram drawn on
yesterday's leftover rows shows queries the code does not make on a clean DB.
Its own name (-otel), not video's petclinic-{shortsha}: that one is shared and
reused across steps, and has no trace store. `vars` prints every host-picked
address as NAME=value — GRAFANA_URL, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, BACKEND_URL,
BASE_URL, API_BASE_URL — which the step exports to every command: the
browser suites and generate.ts read them, the genseq profile's JVM inherits
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT and NOTIFICATIONSERVICE_URL (its visit booking
notifies this instance's service, or AddVisitApiTest's picture loses the
call). `requires` is probed after `up`, with those names
expanded: a stack that came up without the store is a skip saying so.
//select: `select` adds the tests this branch WROTE or EDITED (test-changes.py's
manifest) to the tagged ones, untagged: `{tests.<suite>}` in a command expands
to that suite's picks, each spelled as `item` and joined by `join` — the way
its runner takes them. GENSEQ_SELECT is read by both browser runners
(sequence-tag.ts: <file>::<title>, one per line) and by the JVM's
SequenceTraceExtension (Class#method, the -Dtest syntax). The `when: java` run
boots a Spring context only when there is a JVM test to trace. Capped at 6
(4 browser + 2 JVM) to bound the step's time; a test already tagged takes no slot.
commands: cd petclinic-test && GENSEQ_REFRESH=1 npm run trace:diagram

//: The C4 container view, PROJECTED from the sequence diagrams the step above
draws. Nothing here is a drawing, and every key is optional: with no `c2`
block at all the tab is still built, from the lifelines and arrows alone.
`containers` corrects the only thing a sequence diagram cannot say — what
KIND of thing a lifeline is — and names the stack, which is never guessed.
`drop` on the Java suite is the important one. A C2 shows what is DEPLOYED,
and a @SpringBootTest calling controllers through MockMvc is deployed
nowhere: it is a synthetic client, in-process, with no browser, no socket
and no server. It draws a fine sequence diagram — that is the Sequence
tab's job — and a box here that no operator could point at. The Playwright
suite is the opposite case and stays — but it is not what the box is
called. The container is the BROWSER running the Angular app; Playwright
and Chromium are how this repository happens to drive it in CI, which is
a fact about the test rig and not about anything that ships.
`Test` -> `as` folds the base branch's older participant name in first, so
one `drop` covers a suite that renamed its own lifeline on this branch.
`NotificationService` is a container of its own: a separate JVM on :8090,
reached over HTTP. Its `SMS gateway` stays external — still a log line.
`drawio` is the hand-drawn picture of the same containers, shown under the
projected one: arrows a test walked drawn heavy, the rest grey, and a call the
traces made that no arrow carries added in dashed red. DeploymentDiagramTest
is the guardrail that fails on that red; the page shows where it is.
`Commons` is petclinic-commons, a jar linked into both JVMs: its lifeline is
drawn by ModuleBoundaryTracing for the Sequence tab, and is no container here.
`tests` is here for the TRACES, not for the city: it is the browser run whose
Playwright report the Tests tab harvests, which is why PW_TRACE=on and why the
`traces` step below runs nothing of its own. Recording the same suite twice
would double the longest step on the page for a second, differently-flaky
opinion about the same branch.
It used to carry two more commands and two more keys: an instrumented
`mvn test`, JACOCO_E2E=1 on the acceptance run, a jacoco:merge, plus
`acceptance` and `baseline`. All of that existed for the city's CRAP and
coverage colours, which are switched off in code-city itself now (generate.sh
step [3]) — the four options stay in its COLOR dropdown marked unavailable.
Minutes of Maven and a second Playwright run per review, for two colours
nothing draws any more. The committed coverage-baseline.tsv went with them.
test-on-own-stack.sh: the suite runs against HEAD's own containers (the same
petclinic-<shortsha> instance video.app uses), never against :4200/:8080 — on
23 Sep 2026 those belonged to another checkout and three tests failed against
a backend from a different branch.
COVERAGE_DIR: the same run also measures, per test, which lines each test
executes on both sides — Chromium's JS coverage and a JaCoCo dump of the backend
(test-on-own-stack.sh starts it with --jacoco). `testcov` below harvests it.
tests: cd petclinic-test && PW_TRACE=on COVERAGE_DIR=../.human-review/coverage ./test-on-own-stack.sh npm test
city.title: Code City

//: Playwright's own recordings of the run, carried onto the page so a reviewer
can step through what a test DID without checking the branch out and running
the suite again. Rows land in the Tests tab, beside the covering tests.
`report` is the html reporter's output directory. Nothing is run from here:
the recordings come from the run `city.tests` already does, and the PW_TRACE=on
command turns tracing ON (read by playwright.config.ts).
The .feature scenarios run under cucumber-js, which writes no Playwright
report: src/support/world.ts records one zip + sidecar per scenario into
`cucumber` when PW_TRACE=on, and the command below is that run. It needs
a running stack (SKIP_SERVER_START); test-on-own-stack.sh gives it the same
per-commit instance city.tests just used, not whatever holds :4200.
commands: cd petclinic-test && PW_TRACE=on COVERAGE_DIR=../.human-review/coverage ./test-on-own-stack.sh npm run test:cucumber

//: Which tests execute which changed lines, measured per test — the right-hand
column of the Tests tab. `sources`/`exclude` say what counts as production code;
a changed line outside them (a test, a generated file, a doc) is not counted.
`junit`: {junit} expands to the skill's JUnit Platform listener on the test
classpath; the pom's own jacoco:prepare-agent does the measuring. The backend
suite (JUnit and Cucumber together) runs on a throwaway Postgres, never on the
:5432 every checkout shares (test-on-own-db.sh says why).
`karma`: {karma} expands to the skill's karma config, which loads karma.conf.js.
`e2e`: nothing is run — the browser suites already ran for the traces with
COVERAGE_DIR (city.tests, traces.commands); this reads what they left there.
`app` is how the run gets the application the film is recorded against, and
it exists because the recorder's old liveness check tested the PORT, not the
commit: anything answering on :4200 and :8080 was filmed. This machine keeps
several checkouts of this repository (petclinic, petclinic-main,
petclinic-pr) and each can serve :4200 — so on 17 Sep 2026 a review of
test-pr shipped a film of main, narrated from test-pr's diff, with every
caption asserting what the frames denied.
Now the run owns its own instance: `up` builds the commit under review into
containers of its own and prints the host port it got, `down` runs in a
finally. {sha}/{shortsha} come from `git rev-parse HEAD`, never from here.
--ttl 1800 because this instance exists for one 40-second take; the default
two idle hours would keep a whole stack up long after the film was cut.

app.//db: KEY=value lines (JDBC_URL, DB_HOST_PORT, DB_CONTAINER_PORT, DB_USER, DB_PASSWORD): the review page's Running Database row.

steps.//complexity: Nothing to configure: EndpointComplexityExtractorTest was removed from this repo on 4 Sep 2026, and /human-review measures both sides itself now (endpoint-complexity.py), reading the baseline from the merge-base.

//: The one step that needs BOTH sides of the branch running at the same time,
and that is exactly why it never ran. This block used to say `base-new`
:4300 and `base-old` :4301 — which is not a configuration, it is a promise
about somebody else's machine. Nothing in the pipeline started those two
builds, so the prerequisite found nothing answering, the step was skipped on
every run, and the UX tab arrived empty explaining that it had — on a branch
whose whole subject is the vet field moved onto `app-combo`.
`app` is the same block `video.app` is; "video" borrows it rather than
repeating three commands that would then be two places to forget. The step
expands it TWICE — once with HEAD's {sha}/{shortsha} and once with the
merge-base's — so the two instances are of this branch and of where it
forked, never of whatever a port happens to be serving. Both host ports are
picked by the host (that is what lets two builds of one repo be up at once)
and read back out of what each `up` printed; both are `down`ed in a finally.
//screens: EVERY screen of the app, deep-linked to a seeded row, not the two
somebody guessed the branch touched. The audit shoots them all and
draws only those whose DOM changed; the rest are named in one line.
The list was two entries until 19 Sep 2026, which would have looked
past every list that grew a Vet column — and run-steps.py would have
said so in red, because it follows each changed component to its route.
